intelligence.enrichment: The chapter presents science learning as something that moves beyond reading: learners step out of the book and classroom through activities, experiments, observations, and careful thinking. Because scientific understanding grows through experience, activities and experiments turn ideas in the book into observations that can be questioned and thought through. The learner applies the chapter's view that science learning moves beyond reading into observations, activities, experiments, and careful thinking. If I read the book and know the topic name, I have learned the science; observing and experimenting are optional fun.
